instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'earned it' under my quiz trophy photo. Nobody else buzzed in as decisively as I did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied me pressing the red button. I was testing whether my buzzer worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, checked and ready. The question came straight after, and I answered it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said 'sparrow' before they even showed the bird.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say I recognized it early. Don't write 'lucky guess' under a trophy I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can stop calling my win a gift. I used the same finishing technique as you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied me slowing down. I'd pulled my calf; the others stopped to help me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, controlled pace. I still crossed the line first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I waved you back to help, and you waved at the spectators.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me credit for finishing. You can criticize the wave after you've said I earned the win.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cancelled the outing, following your cross on the booking form. You'll need to tell the team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That cross selected the coach company. You copied it into the cancellation box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, the booking decision. You can explain it; you chose the company.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ring them to restore it, but you tell the team about the mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Make that call with the team here. Then you can explain the cancellation to everyone at once.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the game finished. We said loser washes up, so I'll leave the bowls for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied me laying my king down. I was packing away a spare set; you've resigned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the board. You can clear the bowls while I sort these pieces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. I'll pack the pieces if you do the washing-up you lost.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me pack them. You take the washing-up as your half of clearing up.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a tick beside every sandwich, like you. How far ahead does that put my stall?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those ticks mean gluten-free, not sold. We rank stalls by money raised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, qualifying sandwiches. What do you get for raising the most?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First choice of stall next year. I've raised eighty pounds; you've raised sixty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twenty-one more pounds puts me ahead of you. Does that get first choice, or is someone above us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I joined in when your cousin clapped. Where does that put me for club president?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He was testing the microphone, not applauding. You clapped through the chair's speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, checking the room. What counts toward choosing the next president?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Members vote. My cousin promised to fix the car park; that would save my tyres.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many votes has that car park promise got him compared with me?

cards.title: Enter on My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit them into your side of a contest or bargain before the stakes become fully clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on a blue badge like yours. Let's enter the quiz together before they close the teams.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine says STAFF. I'm here to collect the entry fees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, getting us entered. Put my name beside yours and we'll sort out the fee as a team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twenty pounds each, and the losing team stays to clear the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write our names down before you collect. We can decide who covers what once we're a team.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took my captain's badge off when you took yours off. Let's put both badges on this rematch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine fell off. I was fixing the pin, not giving up the captaincy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, securing it. Winning it back would settle which of us should lead the club.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We captain different teams. Losing a game doesn't make either job vacant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then loser organizes both teams' fixtures next month. Will you play for that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I slid my queen off the board like you did. Let's make this game decide who cooks all weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took my captured queen off. You just removed your best piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, playing with fewer pieces. All the more reason to put something serious on the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're already at a disadvantage. Let's just play for the biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me put the queen back. Will you play for Sunday dinner instead of a biscuit?
